**Complete the global Selmer groups on the frozen RR control pair**

**Disposition:** proposed. **Kind:** research. **Compute class:** new-compute.

Reuse the retained curve maps, verified integral orders and failed certification receipts; supply certified maximal orders and a complete supported squareclass space including class and unit contributions, then impose every required local condition and resolve the true/fake comparison. Do not repeat the closed local panels or call BNF on a merely supplied/partial order. Reuse the successor joined-order bases in det1092_rr_order_join_v1: exact containment and Newton-trace replay improve the order discriminants to22655/37378bits (09/08) without certifying maximality. The later det1092_rr_coprime_support_v1 bases contain the joins and improve the control to28881bits (historical22655bits unchanged); both certifications remain unresolved at22633/28878bits. The third saved order is already contained, so repeating its join is unnecessary.

**Completion evidence:** Both unconditional true Sel_2 groups and maps are certified, with dimensions and quotients by the inherited17- and known rational18-dimensional images, all necessary place coverage, and independently replayable certificates. Unknown dimensions or identical lower bounds do not complete the comparison. Interpret all three dimension comparisons, including a smaller historical-arm dimension. Equality alone is not a realization result: both known rational images already have dimension18 and the pair matches two markings of one elliptic fibre.

**Prerequisites and boundary:** The September14 two-case attempt remains incomplete: all four prime-list order certifications returned unresolved composites. These are not certified field discriminants or proofs of infeasibility. Preserve the exact pair and retrospective same-fibre selection boundary. A changed algorithm needs its own declared resource limits and certificate plan; this work item schedules no campaign. The later joined-order and coprime-support attempts also stop short of maximality. Exact gcd checks show that the new index and saved divisors do not split either remainder; resumption needs an additional certified global-arithmetic method or certificate, not a repeat of those inputs.
